Inline histogram for a numeric vector

Source: R/eda.R
inlhist.Rd

Draws a one-line sketch of a column's distribution, as block characters (or ASCII where the console cannot render them). The point is density of information: a mean and a standard deviation cannot tell you a column is bimodal, skewed or has a gap, and this can, in the width of a table cell. profcols() shows one for every numeric column.

Usage

inlhist(x, bins = 10L)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector.

bins

Number of bins, and so of characters, one positive whole number (default 10).

Value

A length-1 character vector of bins characters.

Details

Non-finite values (NA, NaN, Inf) are dropped. The range of the rest is cut into bins equal-width bins (as graphics::hist() with those breaks) and each bin's count is drawn as one of eight Unicode block heights, scaled to the largest bin; an empty bin is a space, and a bin with any values is at least the lowest block. When the session is not UTF-8, or the environment variable RMBL_ASCII_ONLY is set, five ASCII levels (. : - = #) are used instead. A column with no spread gives one full block in the middle; no finite values give spaces.

Errors: x that is not numeric; bins that is not one positive whole number.

See also

profcols(), which includes one per numeric column.

Examples

set.seed(1)
# A symmetric distribution peaks in the middle.
inlhist(stats::rnorm(1000))
#> [1] "▁▂▄██▇▄▂▁▁"

# A skewed one leans left.
inlhist(stats::rexp(1000))
#> [1] "█▄▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁"

# Bimodality is visible here and in no single summary number.
inlhist(c(stats::rnorm(500, -3), stats::rnorm(500, 3)))
#> [1] "▁▅█▄▁▁▃█▆▁"

# A constant column has no spread to show.
inlhist(rep(5, 10))
#> [1] "     █    "

# more bins for more detail
inlhist(stats::rexp(1000), bins = 30)
#> [1] "█▇▅▄▃▃▂▂▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁▁ ▁ ▁  ▁ ▁"

# text is not a distribution
try(inlhist(c("a", "b")))
#> Error : inlhist: `x` must be numeric, got character
